title: 2006 AMC 8 Problem 12
statement: Antonette gets \(70 \%\) on a \(10\)-problem test, \(80 \%\) on a \(20\)-problem test and \(90 \%\) on a \(30\)-problem test. If the three tests are combined into one \(60\)-problem test, which percent is closest to her overall score?

solutions.text:
Antonette got \(0.7\cdot 10=7\) questions right on the first test. Similarly, she got \(0.8\cdot 20=16\) and \(0.9\cdot 30=27\) problems right on her second and third tests.

Adding these up yields \(50\) correct questions. Her score on the combined test would have been \(100\cdot \dfrac{50}{60}=83\frac{1}{3}\%\), closest to \(83\%\).

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Convert each test percentage into a number of correct answers.
This is a weighted average by number of problems, not a plain average of the three percentages.
